chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
There is no problem if a man slaughters while he is in a state of sexual impurity (junub).

key_terms.جُنُب: Junub — a person in a state of major ritual impurity (janaba), requiring ghusl (ritual bath) before performing acts of worship
key_terms.لَا بَأْس: There is no problem/objection — a standard juridical formula indicating permissibility
key_terms.يَذْبَح: To slaughter/sacrifice an animal in the religiously prescribed manner

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to slaughter an animal while in a state of janaba (sexual impurity) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes a legal ruling that a man in a state of major ritual impurity (janaba) may still perform the ritual slaughtering of animals. This ruling is significant in Islamic jurisprudence (fiqh) because it clarifies that the validity of animal slaughter — unlike acts of worship such as prayer — does not require ritual purity. The original audience of this teaching would have understood this as a clarification for practical daily life situations where obtaining ritual purity (ghusl) before slaughtering might be inconvenient.
word_analysis: in a state of sexual impurity (junub)

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘There is no problem if the man slaughters and he was with sexual impurity’.
en.sarwar: 6. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not unlawful if a person after sexual intercourse and before Ghusl (bath) slaughters an animal.”’
